title: Roman Numerals from I to M
seo_title: Roman Numerals – Primary 4 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Count and write Roman numerals from I to M (1 to 1,000); read clock faces with Roman numerals; convert between Hindu-Arabic and Roman numerals; add and subtract Roman numerals. (summary of the NERDC Primary 4 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 4 maths worksheets on Roman numerals from I to M: symbols, reading and writing Roman numerals, clock faces, converting to and from our numbers and simple addition and subtraction. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: A smaller symbol before a bigger one is subtracted.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Roman numerals use seven symbols: I = 1, V = 5, X = 10, L = 50, C = 100, D = 500, M = 1,000.
  • Add symbols written from big to small: XVI = 10 + 5 + 1 = 16.
  • A smaller symbol before a bigger one is subtracted: IV = 4, IX = 9, XL = 40, XC = 90, CD = 400, CM = 900.

Examples

Example

XLVII

XL = 40, VII = 7

Answer: 47

Example

Write 394

300 = CCC, 90 = XC, 4 = IV

Answer: CCCXCIV

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Writing IIII for 44 is IV.
Reading IX as 11I before X means 10 − 1 = 9.
Using one symbol more than three timesNever write the same symbol four times in a row.

faq.q: Where do we see Roman numerals?
faq.a: On clock faces, chapters of books, names of kings and on buildings.

faq.q: Is there a zero in Roman numerals?
faq.a: No. The Romans had no symbol for zero.

faq.q: What is the biggest number in this topic?

items.q: What number does I stand for?
items.e: I means 1.

items.q: What number does V stand for?
items.e: V means 5. Do not mix it up with X, which means 10.

items.q: What number does X stand for?
items.e: X means 10.

items.q: What number does L stand for?
items.e: L means 50. Do not mix it up with C, which means 100.

items.q: What number does C stand for?
items.e: C means 100. C is the first letter of the Latin word centum, which means a hundred (think of a century).

items.q: Which Roman numeral stands for 50?
Which Roman numeral means 5?
items.e: 5 has its own symbol: V. VX is not a Roman numeral: V is never put before a bigger symbol. IIIII uses 5 Is, but you never write more than 3 of the same symbol in a row.

items.q: What number is III?
items.e: III = 1 + 1 + 1 = 3. It is not 111: each I means 1, wherever it is.

items.q: What number is VII?
What number is XII?
items.e: Split it into tens and units: X = 10 and II = 1 + 1 = 2. So XII = 10 + 2 = 12.

items.q: What number is XV?
items.e: Split it into tens and units: X = 10 and V = 5. So XV = 10 + 5 = 15.

items.q: What number is XI?
items.e: Split it into tens and units: X = 10 and I = 1. So XI = 10 + 1 = 11.

items.q: What number is XVIII?
items.e: Split it into tens and units: X = 10 and VIII = 5 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 8. So XVIII = 10 + 8 = 18.

items.q: What number is XVII?
items.e: Split it into tens and units: X = 10 and VII = 5 + 1 + 1 = 7. So XVII = 10 + 7 = 17.

items.q: Which Roman numeral is 6?
items.e: 6 = 5 + 1, so 6 = VI. IV is 4, because the I comes before the V.

items.q: Which Roman numeral is 8?
items.e: 8 = 5 + 1 + 1 + 1, so 8 = VIII. IIX is wrong: you can only put one I before a bigger symbol.

items.q: Which Roman numeral is 12?
items.e: Partition 12 into 10 + 2. 10 is X and 2 is II. So 12 = XII. III is only 3: the 1 ten must be written X.

items.q: Which Roman numeral is 13?
items.e: Partition 13 into 10 + 3. 10 is X and 3 is III. So 13 = XIII.

items.q: Which Roman numeral is 16?
items.e: Partition 16 into 10 + 6. 10 is X and 6 is VI. So 16 = XVI.

items.q: Which Roman numeral is 20?
What number is IV?
items.e: IV = 5 − 1 = 4. A smaller symbol before a bigger one is taken away, so IV is not 6.

items.q: What number is IX?
items.e: IX = 10 − 1 = 9. A smaller symbol before a bigger one is taken away, so IX is not 11.

items.q: What number is XIV?
items.e: Split it into tens and units: X = 10 and IV = 5 − 1 = 4. So XIV = 10 + 4 = 14. The I comes before the bigger symbol, so take it away. XIV is not 16.

items.q: What number is XIX?
items.e: Split it into tens and units: X = 10 and IX = 10 − 1 = 9. So XIX = 10 + 9 = 19. The I comes before the bigger symbol, so take it away. XIX is not 21.

items.q: What number is XL?
items.e: XL = 50 − 10 = 40. A smaller symbol before a bigger one is taken away, so XL is not 60.

items.q: What number is XC?
items.e: XC = 100 − 10 = 90. A smaller symbol before a bigger one is taken away, so XC is not 110.

items.q: Which Roman numeral means 50?
items.e: 50 has its own symbol: L. LC is not allowed: L is never put before a bigger symbol. C is 100, and XXXXX uses too many Xs.

items.q: What number is XXIV?
items.e: Split it into tens and units: XX = 10 + 10 = 20 and IV = 5 − 1 = 4. So XXIV = 20 + 4 = 24.

items.q: What number is XXXVII?
items.e: Split it into tens and units: XXX = 10 + 10 + 10 = 30 and VII = 5 + 1 + 1 = 7. So XXXVII = 30 + 7 = 37.

items.q: What number is XXXIX?
items.e: Split it into tens and units: XXX = 10 + 10 + 10 = 30 and IX = 10 − 1 = 9. So XXXIX = 30 + 9 = 39.

items.q: What number is CCC?
items.e: CCC = 100 + 100 + 100 = 300. Each C is 100. Do not mix C up with X (10).

items.q: What number is DC?
items.e: DC = 500 + 100 = 600. The smaller C comes after the D, so add it. D is 500, not 1,000 (M) or 50 (L).

items.q: What number is CD?
items.e: CD = 500 − 100 = 400. The smaller C comes before the D, so take it away: CD is not 600.

items.q: What number is CM?
items.e: CM = 1,000 − 100 = 900. The C comes before the M, so take it away: CM is not 1,100.

items.q: What number is DCCC?
items.e: DCCC = 500 + 100 + 100 + 100 = 800. Count the Cs: there are three. D is 500, not 1,000.

items.q: What number is CXX?
items.e: Split it: C = 100; XX = 10 + 10 = 20. So CXX = 100 + 20 = 120. The Xs come after the C, so add them. Roman numerals have no place value, so it is not 102.

items.q: What number is CCLX?
items.e: Split it: CC = 100 + 100 = 200; LX = 50 + 10 = 60. So CCLX = 200 + 60 = 260. LX is 60. XL would be 40.

items.q: What number is CDL?
items.e: Split it: CD = 500 − 100 = 400; L = 50. So CDL = 400 + 50 = 450. CD is 400, not 600, so CDL is not 650.

items.q: What number is DXL?
What number is CCXLV?
Write the number 100 as a Roman numeral.
items.e: Split 100 into 100: C.

items.q: Write the number 42 as a Roman numeral.
items.e: Split 42 into 40 + 2: XLII.

items.q: Write the number 43 as a Roman numeral.
items.e: Split 43 into 40 + 3: XLIII.

items.q: Write the number 80 as a Roman numeral.
items.e: Split 80 into 80: LXXX.

items.q: Write the number 734 as a Roman numeral.
items.e: Split 734 into 700 + 30 + 4: DCCXXXIV.

items.q: Write the number 60 as a Roman numeral.
items.e: Split 60 into 60: LX.

items.q: Write the number 562 as a Roman numeral.
items.e: Split 562 into 500 + 60 + 2: DLXII.

items.q: Write the number 935 as a Roman numeral.
items.e: Split 935 into 900 + 30 + 5: CMXXXV.

items.q: Write the number 3 as a Roman numeral.
items.e: Split 3 into 3: III.

items.q: Write the number 790 as a Roman numeral.
items.e: Split 790 into 700 + 90: DCCXC.

items.q: Write the number 41 as a Roman numeral.
items.e: Split 41 into 40 + 1: XLI.

items.q: Write the number 39 as a Roman numeral.
items.e: Split 39 into 30 + 9: XXXIX.

items.q: Write the number 325 as a Roman numeral.
items.e: Split 325 into 300 + 20 + 5: CCCXXV.

items.q: Write the number 8 as a Roman numeral.
items.e: Split 8 into 8: VIII.

items.q: Write the number 890 as a Roman numeral.
items.e: Split 890 into 800 + 90: DCCCXC.

items.q: Write the number 457 as a Roman numeral.
items.e: Split 457 into 400 + 50 + 7: CDLVII.

items.q: Write the number 109 as a Roman numeral.
items.e: Split 109 into 100 + 9: CIX.

items.q: Write the number 293 as a Roman numeral.
items.e: Split 293 into 200 + 90 + 3: CCXCIII.

items.q: Write the number 724 as a Roman numeral.
items.e: Split 724 into 700 + 20 + 4: DCCXXIV.

items.q: Write the number 47 as a Roman numeral.
items.e: Split 47 into 40 + 7: XLVII.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: XL = 40 and LX = 60. 40 < 60, so XL < LX.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: IX = 9 and XI = 11. 9 < 11, so IX < XI.

items.q: Which Roman numeral is the greatest?
items.e: XXIX = 29, XXXV = 35, XXXVIII = 38, XL = 40. XL is the greatest. A longer numeral is not always bigger.

items.q: Which Roman numeral is the greatest?
items.e: XL = 40, XLVIII = 48, LIV = 54, LX = 60. LX is the greatest. A longer numeral is not always bigger.

items.q: Which Roman numeral is the greatest?
items.e: LXXIX = 79, LXXXV = 85, LXXXVIII = 88, XC = 90. XC is the greatest. A longer numeral is not always bigger.

items.q: Which Roman numeral is the smallest?
items.e: VIII = 8, IX = 9, XI = 11, XII = 12. VIII is the smallest.

items.q: What comes next? XXXVI, XXXVII, XXXVIII, ?
items.e: XXXVI = 36, XXXVII = 37, XXXVIII = 38. The numbers go up in 1s. 38 + 1 = 39 = XXXIX.

items.q: What comes next? XL, L, LX, ?
items.e: XL = 40, L = 50, LX = 60. The numbers go up in 10s. 60 + 10 = 70 = LXX.

items.q: Which list is in order from smallest to largest?
items.e: XVI = 16, XIX = 19, XXI = 21. From smallest to largest: XVI, XIX, XXI.

items.q: Which list is in order from smallest to largest?
items.e: XXXV = 35, XL = 40, L = 50. From smallest to largest: XXXV, XL, L.

items.q: Work out XXIV + VI. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
items.e: XXIV = 24 and VI = 6. 24 + 6 = 30, and 30 = XXX.

items.q: Work out XV + IX. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
items.e: XV = 15 and IX = 9. 15 + 9 = 24, and 24 = XXIV.

items.q: Work out XL + X. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
Work out XXXV + XV. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
Work out L − I. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
items.e: L = 50 and I = 1. 50 − 1 = 49, and 49 = XLIX. IL is not allowed: I can only go before V or X.

items.q: Work out XC − X. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
Work out XIX + XXI. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
items.e: XIX = 19 and XXI = 21. 19 + 21 = 40, and 40 = XL. XXXX is wrong: never write 4 Xs in a row.

items.q: Work out LX − XV. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
items.e: LX = 60 and XV = 15. 60 − 15 = 45, and 45 = XLV. VL is not allowed: only I, X (and C) go before a bigger symbol, and only I before V or X.

items.q: Work out XLV + XLV. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
items.e: XLV = 45 and XLV = 45. 45 + 45 = 90, and 90 = XC. LXXXX is wrong: never write 4 Xs in a row.

items.q: Work out C − I. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
items.e: C = 100 and I = 1. 100 − 1 = 99, and 99 = XCIX. IC is not allowed: I can only go before V or X.
The minute hand (red) points to III, which is quarter past. The hour hand has just passed X (10), so it is quarter past ten. Be careful: X is 10 and XI is 11.
The minute hand (red) points to IX, which is quarter to. The hour hand is nearly at IV (4), so it is quarter to four. Be careful: IV is 4, not 6.

items.q: At the end of a film, Nonso sees “© MCMXCVII”. In what year was the film made?
In what year was this stone laid?
Dayo’s favourite film came out in MCMXCIX and its sequel in MMIX. How many years apart are they?
items.e: MCMXCIX = 1,999 and MMIX = 2,009. 2,009 − 1,999 = 10 years. Reading IX as 11 gives 12 or 8, and forgetting the first M of MCMXCIX gives 1,010.

items.q: M comes from mille, the Latin word for a thousand. Which English word also comes from mille?
items.e: A millennium is 1,000 years. Metre, minute and medium come from other Latin and Greek words.

items.q: Which list of years goes from earliest to latest?
items.e: MCMLX = 1,960, MCMLXX = 1,970, MCMXC = 1,990. From earliest to latest: MCMLX, MCMLXX, MCMXC.

items.q: Work out CM + C. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
items.e: CM = 900 and C = 100. 900 + 100 = 1,000, and 1,000 = M. CMC just puts the numerals side by side. DD is not allowed: D is never repeated.

items.q: Work out M − I. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
items.e: M = 1,000 and I = 1. 1,000 − 1 = 999, and 999 = CMXCIX. IM is not allowed: I can only go before V or X. MI is 1,001.

items.q: Work out D − CC. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
items.e: D = 500 and CC = 200. 500 − 200 = 300, and 300 = CCC. CCD is not a Roman numeral: only one C can go before D. DCC is 500 + 200.

items.q: Work out CDL + L. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
items.e: CDL = 450 and L = 50. 450 + 50 = 500, and 500 = D. CD is 400, not 600, so the answer is not DCC (700).

items.q: Work out C × V. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
items.e: C = 100 and V = 5. 100 × 5 = 500, and 500 = D. CV is 105, not 100 × 5. M is 100 × 10. CCCCC has too many Cs.

items.q: A foundation stone says MCMXXXVI. Kemi reads it as 2,136. What mistake did she make?
c: Added the C instead of taking it away
items.e: MCMXXXVI = M + CM + XXX + VI = 1,000 + 900 + 30 + 6, so the year is 1,936. Adding the C gives 1,000 + 100 + 1,000 + 30 + 6 = 2,136. The C comes before the M, so it must be taken away.

items.q: Which year is not written correctly?
items.e: MIM is not correct: I can only go before V or X. 1,999 is written MCMXCIX. The others are correct: MCMXCIX = 1,999, MCMLXXX = 1,980, MMXX = 2,020.
